Chapter 10: The Long Journey—Grace, Failure, and the Ongoing Formation of Desire.
You know, nobody’s journey is a straight line. Even when we start out with the best intentions, we stumble. We fall back into old habits, and sometimes, we lose sight of what really matters. The truth is, being shaped by love is a slow process—sometimes it’s frustrating, and it never seems completely finished. But here’s the thing: it’s in the messiness of real life that we actually learn the deepest lessons.
Imagine someone trying to build new habits—maybe it’s morning prayer, serving others each week, or just making time to rest on purpose. In the beginning, those routines feel so life-giving. But then, life happens. Stress, disappointment, or even loss can show up and suddenly, the practices slip away. Old desires sneak back in and shame can start to whisper, “Maybe you’ll never change.”
But that’s not where the story ends. Right in the middle of failure, there’s an invitation—a chance to experience grace. It’s about being willing to start again, forgiving yourself, and letting others walk with you. Those are the habits that build a heart that doesn’t give up easily. Over time, you realize that this journey isn’t about being perfect—it’s about sticking with it.
Most of us carry wounds—old patterns, regrets, maybe even fears that shape the things we love. The real journey of spiritual formation isn’t about erasing those scars. It’s about learning how to love, even with them. Habits like confession, forgiveness, and gratitude become tools for healing. They remind us that hearts can be reshaped, no matter how many times they’ve been broken.
It’s so easy to focus on what’s visible—the changed routines, new behaviors, all those outward signs of growth. But the real work is happening underneath, where you can’t always see it. That’s where desire itself is being reshaped, slowly and quietly.
The journey’s long. There will be setbacks. But with grace, patience, and the support of a community, your heart really can be formed for love.
So here’s the invitation: keep going. Trust that every small step, every new habit, every moment of grace is part of your story. This journey isn’t about arriving—it’s about becoming. And in the end, it’s love that shapes our hearts, one day at a time.
